data.narrative:
Orangewood Labs is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable in the same sector, including Series A–B stage firms such as Humanoid ($1.4B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), as well as earlier-stage reference points like Walden Robotics ($1.1B seed valuation).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling, anchored to a $30M total-raised proxy and applying a typical 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $60M. Peer-median analysis across the five most comparable same-sector companies yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The wide spread reflects stage heterogeneity in the peer set, with three comps at Series B and one at seed stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $855M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects uncertainty around whether Orangewood's technology trajectory and market position align with peers now valued at scale. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to the peer cohort, competitive differentiation in manufacturing robotics, and the appropriate stage-adjustment discount to apply to Series B valuations.
